read.sections.0.heading.source: The jobs behind an AI tool
read.sections.0.heading.back: The jobs behind an AI tool

read.sections.0.text.source: An AI tool can seem to work by itself, but many people help to make it. For some kinds of training, workers add a label to each example, such as “bus” or “tree” for a photo. Other workers rate a tool's answers, so it can be tested and improved. Moderators check harmful posts, so a tool learns what it must not show. Many tools also learned from writing and pictures found online. In 2023, some writers and artists said nobody had asked them first. Some went to court, and courts are still deciding these cases.
read.sections.0.text.back: An AI tool can look as if it works by itself, but many people help to make it. For some kinds of training, workers add a label to each example, for example “bus” or “tree” for a photo. Other workers rate a tool's answers, so the tool can be tested and improved. Moderators check harmful posts, so a tool learns what it must not show. Many tools also learned from writing and pictures found on the internet. In 2023, some writers and artists said that nobody had asked their permission first. Some of them sued in court, and those cases have still not been decided.
read.sections.0.text.note: "Courts are still deciding these cases" as "perkara-perkara itu masih belum diputuskan" (those cases are still not decided), which says the same more simply.

read.sections.0.simpler.source: Many people help to make AI tools. For some training, workers add a label to each example. A photo may get the label “bus” or “tree”. Other workers check if its answers are good. Moderators check posts that could hurt people. Many tools also learned from words and pictures online. In 2023, some writers and artists said nobody asked them. Some went to court. Courts are still deciding.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: Many people help to make AI tools. For some training, workers add a label to each example. A photo may get the label “bus” or “tree”. Other workers check whether the tool's answers are good. Moderators check posts that could hurt people. Many tools also learned from words and pictures on the internet. In 2023, some writers and artists said nobody asked their permission. Some went to court. The courts have not finished deciding.

read.sections.1.text.source: Like clothes, an AI tool has a supply chain. A company that builds a tool often pays another firm, or an online platform, to find workers. Many of them live far away, in countries such as Kenya and the Philippines. In January 2023, a news magazine reported on about three dozen workers in Kenya. In 2021 and 2022, they labelled harmful text for a well-known AI tool. They took home about 1.32 to 2 US dollars an hour. The AI company paid the firm in the middle 12.50 dollars an hour for their work. The firm said this also paid for offices, managers and other costs. In August 2023, a newspaper spoke to 36 online workers in the Philippines. All but two said some of their pay came late, was cut or never came. Their platform said this was rare. These reports describe certain workers and firms, not every AI job.
read.sections.1.text.back: Like clothes, an AI tool has a supply chain. The company that makes a tool often pays another company, or an online platform, to find workers. Many of those workers live far away, in countries such as Kenya and the Philippines. In January 2023, a news magazine reported on about thirty-some workers in Kenya. In 2021 and 2022, they labelled harmful text for a well-known AI tool. They took home about 1.32 to 2 US dollars an hour. The AI company paid the go-between company 12.50 dollars an hour for their work. The go-between company said that money was also used for offices, managers and other costs. In August 2023, a newspaper spoke with 36 online workers in the Philippines. All except two said some of their pay was late, cut or never paid. Their platform said this rarely happens. These reports describe certain workers and companies, not every AI job.
read.sections.1.text.note: "About three dozen" as "sekitar tiga puluhan" (about thirty-some). "The firm in the middle" as "perusahaan perantara" (go-between company), as before. "Platform" is kept: it is the new key word and the everyday Indonesian word for an online platform. Decimal commas (1,32; 12,50).

read.sections.1.simpler.source: An AI tool has a supply chain, like clothes. The company often pays another firm or a platform to find workers. Many live far away, in Kenya, the Philippines and other places. In 2023, a magazine wrote about Kenyan workers. They labelled harmful text for an AI tool. They got less than 2 US dollars an hour. The AI firm paid 12.50 dollars an hour to the firm in the middle. That firm said the money also paid other costs. A newspaper spoke to 36 workers in the Philippines. Nearly all said some pay was late, cut or missing. Their platform said this was rare. The reports are about some workers, not all.
read.sections.1.simpler.back: An AI tool has a supply chain, like clothes. Its company often pays another company or a platform to find workers. Many workers live far away, in Kenya, the Philippines and other places. In 2023, a magazine wrote about workers in Kenya. They labelled harmful text for an AI tool. They got less than 2 US dollars an hour. The AI company paid 12.50 dollars an hour to the go-between company. That company said the money was also used for other costs. A newspaper spoke with 36 workers in the Philippines. Nearly all said some of their pay was late, cut or missing. Their platform said this rarely happens. These reports are about some workers, not all of them.

read.sections.2.heading.source: An old pattern, and a new study
read.sections.2.heading.back: An old pattern, and a new study

read.sections.2.text.source: Low pay for each small piece of work is not new. In the 1800s, people in England called very low-paid, hard work “sweating”, and later spoke of a sweatshop. Workers and reformers pushed for change. In 1909, a British law set a minimum wage in four trades, such as tailoring and making chains. In 2023, researchers at the University of Oxford checked 15 online work platforms. Some of them sell AI data work. The researchers looked at pay, conditions, contracts, management and a voice for workers. None met their basic standards, and the best scored 5 out of 10. They also asked 250 people who do small online tasks about their work. On average, these workers earned about 2.15 US dollars an hour. More than a quarter of their time was unpaid, such as time spent looking for tasks. After the study, some platforms changed their rules, for example by setting a minimum wage.
read.sections.2.text.back: Low pay for each small piece of work is not new. In the 1800s, people in England called hard work with very low pay “sweating”, and later talked about sweatshops. Workers and reformers pushed for change. In 1909, an English law set a minimum wage in four fields of work, such as sewing clothes and making chains. In 2023, researchers at the University of Oxford checked 15 online work platforms. Some of these platforms sell data work for AI. The researchers looked at pay, working conditions, contracts, management and a voice for workers. None met their basic standards, and the best score was 5 out of 10. They also asked 250 people who do small tasks online about their work. On average, these workers got about 2.15 US dollars an hour. More than a quarter of their time was not paid, for example time spent looking for tasks. After the study, some platforms changed their rules, for example by setting a minimum wage.
read.sections.2.text.note: "Sweatshop" stays in English, with "sweating" glossed "berkeringat" (TERMS.md). "A British law" as "undang-undang Inggris": Indonesian usually says "Inggris" for Britain; "Britania Raya" is the formal name if reviewers prefer it. "Reformers" as "para pembaru"; "tailoring" as "menjahit pakaian" (sewing clothes).

watch.summary.source: In this news interview, a reporter talks with an expert. The expert works for a group that wants AI to be used in a fair way. She explains that AI tools need lots of data. A computer does not know by itself if a picture shows a cat or a dog. People must look at the pictures and label them, again and again. Then the tool can learn. A lot of this work is done online, in poorer parts of the world, because the pay there is lower. Some workers must look at harmful posts, so other people don't have to see them. The pay is often very low. Workers are not always sure they will be paid. The expert says AI is really built on human work and human thinking. She hopes for clear rules to protect these workers.
watch.summary.back: In this news interview, a reporter speaks with an expert. That expert works at a group that wants AI to be used in a fair way. She explains that AI tools need lots of data. A computer does not know by itself whether a picture shows a cat or a dog. People must look at those pictures and label them, again and again. Then the tool can learn. Much of this work is done online, in poorer parts of the world, because the pay there is lower. Some workers must look at harmful posts, so that other people don't need to see them. The pay is often very low. Workers are not always sure that they will be paid. The expert says that AI is really built on human work and human thinking. She hopes there will be clear rules to protect these workers.

sensitiveNotes.1.source: Work and money: many learners can't work legally, and people close to them may do low-paid, informal or online work. Never ask about learners' or their families' jobs, pay or money. Keep the discussion on the made-up Ask Me workers and the reported facts. Words like “sweatshop” and “unfair pay” may feel close to home; let learners speak if they want to, without pressing.
sensitiveNotes.1.back: Work and money: many learners are not allowed to work officially by law, and people close to them may do low-paid, informal or online work. Never ask about the jobs, pay or money of learners or their families. Keep the discussion on the made-up Ask Me workers and the reported facts. Words like “sweatshop” and “unfair pay” may feel close to their lives; let learners speak if they want to, without pressing.

educatorNotes.0.source: The facts are dated and their scope matters; each report describes particular workers, firms, platforms and years, not every AI job. Kenya: TIME (Billy Perrigo, 18 January 2023) reported that about three dozen workers at an outsourcing firm's Nairobi office labelled harmful text for a safety filter from November 2021 to early 2022 and took home about $1.32 to $2 an hour; the AI company's contracts paid the firm $12.50 an hour. The firm said that rate covered all its costs (offices, salaries, benefits) and that workers earned $1.46 to $3.74 an hour after tax; TIME's sources disputed that. Philippines: The Washington Post (Rebecca Tan and Regine Cabato, August 2023) spoke to 36 current and former freelancers on one platform; 34 said payments had been delayed, reduced or cancelled, and the platform said delays were “exceedingly rare”. The companies (OpenAI, Sama, Scale AI and its Remotasks platform) are named only in sources and here, as the Digital World spec asks. Writers' and artists' work: in 2023 some writers and artists sued AI companies or signed petitions asking for consent, credit and pay. The companies did not all take one position: some argued that training on such material is lawful (fair use in the US) or said they used licensed and public material, some declined to comment, and one news agency licensed its archive to an AI company (Anchorage Daily News, from The Washington Post, 16 July 2023). Court cases have moved on since; check the latest before teaching that part, and don't tell learners that all creative work was taken without asking. The claim record is in content/courses/digital-world/claims/DW05.md.
educatorNotes.0.back: These facts are dated, and their scope matters; each report describes particular workers, companies, platforms and years, not every AI job. The company said that rate covered all its costs (offices, salaries, benefits) and that workers got 1.46 to 3.74 dollars an hour after tax; TIME's sources disputed this. Philippines: The Washington Post (Rebecca Tan and Regine Cabato, August 2023) spoke with 36 freelancers who still or once worked on one platform; 34 said their payments had been delayed, reduced or cancelled, and the platform said delays were “very rare”. The companies (OpenAI, Sama, Scale AI and its Remotasks platform) are named only in the sources and here, as the Digital World spec asks. Writers' and artists' work: in 2023, some writers and artists sued AI companies or signed petitions asking for consent, credit and pay. The companies did not all take one position: some argued that training models on such material is lawful (fair use in the United States) or said they used licensed and public material, some would not comment, and one news agency licensed its archive to an AI company (Anchorage Daily News, from The Washington Post, 16 July 2023). Court cases have developed since then; check the latest before teaching that part, and don't tell learners that all creative work was taken without permission. The claim record is in content/courses/digital-world/claims/DW05.md.

educatorNotes.1.source: Fairwork's Cloudwork Ratings 2023 (Oxford Internet Institute, 20 July 2023) scored 15 online freelance and microwork platforms on five principles (fair pay, conditions, contracts, management and representation); scores ran from 0 to 5 out of 10 (Comeup, Prolific and Terawork highest; Amazon Mechanical Turk, Freelancer, Microworkers and Workana at 0), and none met its minimum standards. Not all of them sell AI work; the microwork platforms (Appen, Scale/Remotasks and others) sell data labelling, model evaluation and content moderation to AI companies. Its survey (February to May 2023) heard from 752 workers in 94 countries and says it does not aim to be representative; the 250 microworkers among them (51 countries) averaged $50.30 a week, which Fairwork gives as about $2.15 an hour, and 26.85% of their platform time was unpaid (looking for tasks, unpaid tests, applying). Four platforms made 17 changes after Fairwork's suggestions, and two adopted minimum-wage policies. The report itself says that “precarious piece-rate work has a long legacy”. The 1909 Trade Boards Act set legally enforceable minimum wages in chainmaking, lace finishing, paper box making and ready-made tailoring (Modern Records Centre, University of Warwick); “sweater” was used in England by 1850 and “sweating” spread in the 1880s (Britannica).
educatorNotes.1.back: Fairwork's Cloudwork Ratings 2023 (Oxford Internet Institute, 20 July 2023) scored 15 online freelance and microwork platforms on five principles (fair pay, working conditions, contracts, management and worker representation); scores ran from 0 to 5 out of 10 (Comeup, Prolific and Terawork highest; Amazon Mechanical Turk, Freelancer, Microworkers and Workana got 0), and none met its minimum standards. Not all of them sell AI work; the microwork platforms (Appen, Scale/Remotasks and others) sell data labelling, model evaluation and content moderation services to AI companies. Its survey (February to May 2023) heard from 752 workers in 94 countries and states it is not meant to represent all workers; the 250 microworkers among them (from 51 countries) got on average 50.30 US dollars a week, which Fairwork puts at about 2.15 dollars an hour, and 26.85% of their time on the platforms was unpaid (looking for tasks, unpaid tests, applying). Four platforms made 17 changes after Fairwork's suggestions, and two adopted minimum-wage policies. The report itself says that “uncertain piece-rate work has a long history”. The 1909 Trade Boards Act set legally binding minimum wages in chainmaking, lace finishing, paper box making and ready-made clothes tailoring (Modern Records Centre, University of Warwick); the word “sweater” was already used in England in 1850, and “sweating” spread in the 1880s (Britannica).
educatorNotes.1.note: The report's quoted words ("precarious piece-rate work has a long legacy") are translated; "kerja borongan" is the usual Indonesian for piece-rate work. Reviewers may prefer the English in brackets.
